correctness.rationale: The sign-invariance, constructive legal canonical sorting in every fiber, exhaustive classification of two singleton sign classes, and explicit safe crossings of every quotient-cube coordinate reconstruct a complete proof for every n>=4; n=3 handled separately. The awkward j=i-1 case is repaired by one legal adjacent swap, with the c(i)!=i+1 sublemma verified from sorted L/R blocks. Separate Python and C++17 implementations check all graph properties to n=8/9, and all constructive signatures to n=14; a nonisometric six-symbol witness has a seven-move route and inversion lower bound.

originality.rationale: The exact graph is the induced subgraph of the adjacent-transposition permutohedron on derangements, with a distinct range-two supergraph. Baril–Vajnovszki use unrestricted and occasionally multiple swaps/three-cycles; Jain proves connectivity for arbitrary transpositions and explicitly notes adjacent-swap frozen states, which are not new. Neither inspected primary result provides the all-order \(2^{n-2}\) component partition, its complete left/right invariants and two unique isolated vertices, or the sharp distance-two hypercube quotient. Matching-object and stronger-implication checks, semantic research-record searches, and direct literature/OEIS index searches revealed no covering theorem. Priority remains qualified for unindexed work.

value.rationale: A natural no-fixed-point/forbidden-diagonal constraint induces a nontrivial locality-dependent reconfiguration problem. The theorem supplies a complete infinite family component invariant, shows the exact unique frozen states, proves that enlarging allowable swap distance from one to two is sufficient and necessary for connectivity at all n>=4, and identifies the entire quotient as a hypercube. The metric counterexample confirms this is not a routine isometric restriction of the permutohedron; it provides a structured benchmark for local assignment transformations rather than a mere enumeration of derangements.
